record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Given a parametrizable algebraic surface X, design an efficient algorithm that finds a parametrization of X.

evidence.quote: There are no analogue results for higher dimensional varieties, even though there have been some attempts for algebraic surfaces.
Problem 21. Let X be a parametric algebraic surface. Design an algorithm which finds a parametrization of X .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X \subset \mathbb{A}^n_k$ (or $\mathbb{P}^n_k$) be an irreducible algebraic surface that is parametrizable, i.e., there exists a dominant rational map $\varphi: \mathbb{A}^2_k \dashrightarrow X$ given by rational functions in two parameters whose image is Zariski-dense in $X$. Equivalently, the function field $k(X)$ is a purely transcendental extension of $k$ of transcendence degree two.

Design an efficient algorithm which, given as input the defining ideal (or implicit equations) of such a surface $X$, decides parametrizability and, when $X$ is parametrizable, outputs an explicit rational parametrization $\varphi(s,t) = (\varphi_1(s,t), \ldots, \varphi_n(s,t)) \in k(s,t)^n$ of $X$. The algorithm should work for arbitrary parametrizable algebraic surfaces (not only special classes such as quadrics, cubics, or surfaces of fixed degree), and its complexity should be analyzed.
artifact.status_search_result: Algorithms for parametrizing rational algebraic surfaces have been developed, notably by Schicho (1998) who gave a general algorithm for rational surfaces, and by Sendra and collaborators who treated properness, inversion, and radical parametrizations. However, designing a uniformly efficient algorithm for arbitrary parametrizable surfaces remains an active topic, and follow-up work on radical parametrizations and reparametrization continues. The problem is thus partially solved: existence of algorithms is known, but efficiency and full generality are still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Rational Parametrization of Surfaces (Schicho)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm by Schicho for computing rational parametrizations of rational surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: A general algorithm to parametrize rational surfaces exists.

status_evidence.title: First steps towards radical parametrization of algebraic surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Sendra and Sevilla initiate the study of radical parametrizations of surfaces, extending the rational case.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on extending parametrization algorithms beyond the rational case.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic and algorithmic aspects of radical parametrizations
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms to implicitize radical parametrizations and to test reparametrization into rational ones.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic aspects of surface parametrization are still under active development.
